analysis.title: Midday Market Intelligence: inches
key_insights: On Monday 9 November at 12:12 PM ET the S&P 500 was +2.3%, helped by lower oil prices. The VIX stayed elevated at 25 and the 10-year Treasury yield rose a bit to 4.88%. Markets are still assessing the post-midterm-election landscape ahead of this week's CPI, with 3Q earnings season ongoing.
The tape is pro-cyclical. Consumer Staples is the only S&P 500 sector underperforming. Industrials, Consumer Discretionary, Communication Services and Tech are leading the index higher.
GS expects volatility to persist as the market keeps debating the AI trade. Its stated frame is that AI is not the economy and the market is not all AI.
Last week's economic updates were mixed. October payrolls beat expectations at +165k with unemployment down 10bps to 4.1%. Fiscal deficits remain a growth challenge and business sentiment was mixed.

GS forecasts October core CPI at +0.16% (consensus +0.2%) and headline CPI at +0.21% (consensus +0.3%). This is consistent with a larger +0.23% core PCE increase in October and is largely driven by higher food and energy prices. Items to watch are airfares, medical service prices and auto inflation. CPI is due Tuesday.
Consumer Discretionary is among the best performers today, helped by lower oil prices and the strong payrolls report.

Apparel retailers RL, TPR, UAA and KTB reported last week and showed a generally resilient consumer. GS sees growing divergence between names exposed to accessible luxury with strong brands (RL, TPR) and names dependent on department stores and mass wholesale (UAA, KTB).
WYNN's 3Q26 earnings came in below both GS and consensus expectations. The company cited improving Las Vegas trends and said Wynn Al Marjan in the UAE is still on track to open in September 2027.

Bonnie Herzog is incrementally positive on EL after a China trip. She cites its 'Beauty Reimagined' vision, a faster innovation-led go-to-market strategy and continued share gains in China and beyond.

Jim Schneider's note says the market is questioning the magnitude of the 2028 data center build, but GS thinks risk/reward in semis is now compelling after the sector-wide pullback. GS leans into AI compute leaders NVDA, AVGO and AMD and semi-cap equipment makers AMAT and LRCX to capture the capacity ramp.

Chart of the Day: Guillaume Jaisson sees European indices as relatively attractive as the AI trade is questioned. AI Infrastructure is c.15% of the STOXX 600 but only 2pp of its expected 9% 2027 earnings growth, so the region offers more diversified performance than the AI-sensitive S&P 500.

GS suggests leaning into European infrastructure suppliers as capex growth peaks. It also suggests looking for contrarian opportunities in European Software and IT Services that show evidence of AI monetization.
Calendar: October CPI on Tuesday. After the close today OXY, NGS, RNGR, RKLB, LINE, EQPT, CHRS, TTD, TTWO, ZIP and CWST report. TDG, VG and JBI report before the open Tuesday.
